title: SQL to CSV Converter – INSERT Statements to CSV | OpenAnyDoc
description: Convert a SQL dump to CSV in your browser: CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements run in a SQL engine on your device, and the biggest table becomes a CSV.
heading: SQL to CSV Converter: INSERT Rows to a Table
subtitle: Drop a .sql file or paste SQL and its largest table opens as CSV; nothing is uploaded.
intro: Convert SQL to CSV in your browser: drop a .sql file or paste CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements, and they run in a SQL engine inside this page. The table with the most rows opens in the CSV viewer to check, edit and download. MySQL dumps are tidied first: backtick quotes, ENGINE= and AUTO_INCREMENT. Nothing is uploaded, and no database server is involved.

stepsTitle: How it works: convert SQL to CSV

steps.title: Open or paste your SQL
steps.text: Drop a .sql file, choose it, paste SQL into the paste box, or try one of the samples.

steps.title: The statements run in your browser
steps.text: CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements run in a SQL engine inside your browser. The table with the most rows becomes the CSV.

steps.title: Check and edit
steps.text: The table opens in the CSV viewer: sort, filter, edit cells and undo before you save.

steps.title: Download
steps.text: Download saves a .csv file; the viewer can also save it as Excel, Markdown, HTML or SQL.

handlesTitle: What the SQL to CSV converter handles
handles: Input: a .sql file or pasted SQL.
Statements: CREATE TABLE and INSERT, run by a SQL engine in your browser.
MySQL dumps: backtick quotes, ENGINE= and AUTO_INCREMENT tidied first.
Several tables: the one with the most rows becomes the CSV.
Output: a table in the CSV viewer, saved as CSV, Excel, Markdown, HTML or SQL.
limits: Stored procedures, PostgreSQL COPY ... FROM stdin blocks and other dialect-specific syntax are not supported; an error is shown.
Only one table becomes the CSV: the one with the most rows.
faqTitle: SQL to CSV: questions and answers

faq.question: Is my file uploaded?
faq.answer: No. The statements run inside your browser on your device; nothing is sent to a server, and pasted SQL stays in this tab.

faq.question: Which table becomes the CSV?
faq.answer: The table with the most rows after all the statements have run. Its columns come from its CREATE TABLE statement.

faq.question: Does it work with a MySQL dump?
faq.answer: Yes for tables and INSERT statements. Backtick quotes, ENGINE= and AUTO_INCREMENT are tidied before the dump runs.

faq.question: Does it work with a PostgreSQL dump?
faq.answer: INSERT statements work, but COPY ... FROM stdin blocks are not supported and show an error. Export the data as INSERT statements instead (pg_dump --inserts).

faq.question: Is a database server needed?
faq.answer: No. A built-in SQL engine runs inside this page, so there is nothing to install or connect to.

faq.question: What happens when a statement fails?
faq.answer: The page shows the error instead of a table. Stored procedures and other syntax specific to one database are the usual cause.

faq.question: How do I convert a SQL file to CSV?
faq.answer: Run the SQL file's CREATE TABLE and INSERT statements in a database, then export the table as CSV. OpenAnyDoc does both in your browser: open the .sql file or paste the statements, and the table with the most rows opens in the CSV viewer, ready to download, with no database server and no upload.
